_comment: Term glossary for hooks/locales, used by client/src/scripts/translate.mjs's --dir pipeline. It carries two kinds of entry. (1) Self-mappings: protocol literals that hooks/locales/zh.json embeds as fixed tokens the AI or the user must reply/see verbatim — the LLM must copy them through unchanged rather than translate them. See hooks/locales/en.json, where the same literals already survive untranslated in the hand-authored English (e.g. compliance.idNote keeps the Chinese word 誤判 even in English, because it is the fixed phrase the user is told to reply with regardless of locale). (2) Negation-carrying clauses: a notice whose entire job is to say a check did NOT happen becomes an all-clear if the negation is lost, and a machine whose OS locale is ja gets Japanese with no opt-in. In v1.26.174 that happened for real — zh.json bracketed its negations for emphasis (「沒有」被把關) and the pipeline rendered the bracket contents as a standalone noun, detaching the negation from the predicate. v1.30.1 rewrote those sentences so the negation is plain rather than bracketed, and replaced the single ⚠️ with 🟢/🟡/🔴 status lights (green = OwnMind did its job, including blocking; yellow = reduced protection or worth a look; red = did not run / did not check / misconfigured); these clauses are pinned whole anyway, because the failure was silent and the cost of it recurring is a user reading 'not protected' as 'protected'. Both classes are belt-and-braces with hooks/locales/ja.override.json (which forces the final value regardless of what the LLM returns) and tests/hook-locales-ja-meaning.test.js (which fails if a value stops denying what the English denies).

zh-to-en.沒有照你的規矩檢查過: was not checked against your rules
zh-to-en.沒被你的規矩擋過就跑了: ran without your rules ever checking it

zh-to-ja.沒有照你的規矩檢查過: ルールに照らしてチェックされていません
zh-to-ja.沒有檢查過: チェックされていません
zh-to-ja.沒被你的規矩擋過就跑了: ルールのチェックを一度も受けずに実行されました
